headline: TSA daily travelers: 2.85% below a year earlier in 2026Q3; 0.66% below a year earlier in 2026Q2.
plain_summary: TSA publishes how many people pass through its airport checkpoints each day. This file runs from 2019-01-01 to 2026-10-08: 2,838 days, with no date missing. In July to September 2026 TSA screened an average of 2.51 million travelers a day, 2.85% below the same period a year earlier (92 days against 92). In April to June 2026 TSA screened an average of 2.57 million travelers a day, 0.66% below the same period a year earlier (91 days against 91). The 7-day average ending 2026-10-08 is 2.50 million a day, 2.05% below the same weekdays 364 days earlier. Across the 9 quarters from 2024Q2 to 2026Q2 that the pandemic does not touch, the correlation of TSA growth with United's growth is 0.44 for capacity (n=9), 0.06 for traffic (n=9), -0.32 for unit revenue (n=9). The count covers every airline and airport and counts people screened, not tickets or revenue.

source.series: TSA checkpoint travel numbers, people screened per day

definitions.travelers_7d: Mean of the 7 calendar days ending on the date. Null unless all 7 days are present.
definitions.yoy_7d: travelers_7d divided by travelers_7d 364 days earlier, minus 1. 364 days is 52 weeks, so both windows hold the same weekdays. Uses no count dated after the date.
definitions.mean_daily_travelers: Mean of the daily counts published in the month or quarter.
definitions.yoy: mean_daily_travelers divided by the mean of the same period a year earlier, minus 1. For a period the data ends inside, the prior-year mean runs from the period's start to the same month and day only. Null when the prior-year window is missing a day.
definitions.days_used: Days with a count behind mean_daily_travelers; prior_days_used is the same for the prior-year mean.
definitions.vs_2019: mean_daily_travelers divided by the same quarter of 2019.
definitions.pandemic: True from 2020Q1 until the first complete quarter with vs_2019 at or above 1.
definitions.yoy_base_pandemic: True when the same quarter a year earlier is a pandemic quarter.

quarterly.yoy_basis: start of period to the same month and day a year earlier

columns.tsa_yoy: TSA mean daily travelers, growth on the same quarter a year earlier
columns.ual_asm_yoy: United available seat miles (capacity), same comparison
columns.ual_rpm_yoy: United revenue passenger miles (traffic), same comparison
columns.ual_trasm_yoy: United total revenue per available seat mile (unit revenue), same comparison

correlation.rule: Complete quarters where neither the quarter nor the same quarter a year earlier is a pandemic quarter.

other_samples.rule: Complete quarters that are not pandemic quarters; growth measured against a pandemic quarter stays in.
Every complete quarter with a growth rate, pandemic quarters included.

versus_united.note: Pearson correlation of the quarterly growth rates. United's growth compares each quarter's earnings-release figure with the figure released for the same quarter a year earlier. The non_pandemic sample was fixed before any correlation was computed; the other two samples are listed so the choice can be checked.

monthly_control.yoy_basis: start of period to the same month and day a year earlier

limits: The count is TSA's national total: all airlines and all airports with a TSA checkpoint. It is not a United figure and says nothing about United's share.
It counts people screened at checkpoints, not tickets, fares, miles flown or revenue.
United's ASM, RPM and TRASM cover its whole network, including flights that start outside the United States, where TSA does not screen.
The series starts on 2019-01-01, so it cannot inform the 2013-2019 fit period, and year-over-year growth starts in 2020.

TSA revises the numbers. This file holds the values served on the retrieval dates listed under inputs, not the values first published. TSA page note: "Passenger travel numbers are updated Monday through Friday by 9 a.m. Travel numbers during holiday weeks though may be slightly delayed." TSA page note: "Archived Data has been updated including Known Crewmembers and later flight travel numbers."

The running year comes from TSA's running-year page and earlier years from its per-year archive pages. Growth for the running year therefore compares a page TSA may still revise with pages it has already revised; the stored pages do not show how large such a revision is.

Pandemic quarters (2020Q1 to 2023Q1) are marked: a quarter is marked from 2020Q1 until the mean is back at or above the same quarter of 2019. Growth in 2023Q2 to 2024Q1 is measured against a pandemic quarter and is marked yoy_base_pandemic.

The daily growth rate compares with 364 days earlier, which lines up weekdays but not holidays: a holiday that falls in a different week than a year before moves the rate for reasons other than demand.
Month and quarter growth compares calendar periods, so the two years can differ in their mix of weekdays and by a leap day.
2026Q4 is incomplete (8 of 92 days); its growth compares the prior year from the quarter's start to the same month and day.
This is an observed series, not a forecast. Nothing here predicts future travel.
The United correlation rests on 9 quarters. It describes those quarters and does not establish that TSA volume drives United's results.
